label: prop:mass-element-nf
title: Normal form of the Hecke mass element
html:
The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_3(R, q) (Hecke mass element) has a specific normal form structure determined by the word length filtration on the NF basis.

Statement

Proposition (conditional on conj:mass-endomorphism). For any particle with braid representative \beta in H_3(R, q), the Hecke mass element has the NF decomposition:

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)
  =
  a_1(\beta)\,(\sigma_0 + \sigma_1)
  +
  a_3(\beta)\,(L_+ + L_-)
  +
  a_5(\beta)\, e^-

with a_0 = 0 (\gamma coefficient vanishes). The coefficients a_1, a_3, a_5 > 0 depend on the specific particle through its brane tower weights.

Vanishing of \gamma (photon masslessness)

The descent involution \hat\tau_n at the first brane level projects onto the H_1(q) content of H_3(R, q). Since H_1(q) = \mathrm{span}\{\gamma\} (the identity is the only degree-0 element), the descended component at level 0 is \gamma. The transient component at level 0 therefore has zero \gamma coefficient — it lives in \ker(\hat\tau_0) = \mathrm{span}\{\sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+, L_-, e^-\}.

Since all brane levels n \geq 1 contribute to \ker(\hat\tau_{n-1}), and the accumulated mass element is the sum over all levels, the total \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}} inherits a_0 = 0 from the first-level filtration.

This is the NF statement that the photon is massless: the mass endomorphism has zero projection onto \gamma.

Degree filtration and cycling

The NF basis has word lengths (degrees):

Degree Basis elements Tower levels
0 \gamma Descended (killed)
1 \sigma_0, \sigma_1 n = 1, 4, 7, \ldots
2 L_+, L_- n = 2, 5, 8, \ldots
3 e^- n = 3, 6, 9, \ldots

The descent involution at level n kills elements of degree \leq (n-1) \bmod 3, so the transient contribution at level n lives in degree (n \bmod 3) elements. The tower cycles through degrees 1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 1 \to 2 \to 3 \to \cdots, accumulating contributions to \sigma_i, then L_\pm, then e^-, repeating.

Explicit NF for the electron

For the electron (trefoil, \mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2})/\hbar_q^2 mass formula), grouping the \mathrm{Li}_2 series by n \bmod 3:

  S_k = \sum_{\substack{n \geq 1 \\ n \equiv k \pmod{3}}}
  \frac{q^{-2n}}{n^2},
  \qquad k \in \{1, 2, 0\}

gives:

Group Contributes to Fraction of \mathrm{Li}_2 NF coefficient
S_1 (n = 1, 4, 7, \ldots) \sigma_0, \sigma_1 76.9\% a_1 \approx 86.2
S_2 (n = 2, 5, 8, \ldots) L_+, L_- 16.7\% a_3 \approx 37.4
S_0 (n = 3, 6, 9, \ldots) e^- 6.4\% a_5 \approx 13.4

The electron mass is mostly carried by the crossing channels (\sigma_0, \sigma_1), not by the trefoil channel itself. The e^- coefficient (\approx 13.4 including the descended part) is only 12\% of the total mass element norm.

Witness: computed from \mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2}) grouping at q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps).
